status.summary: Former UFC light heavyweight champion. He won the belt from Alex Pereira by unanimous decision at UFC 313 (Mar 8, 2025) and lost it in the UFC 320 rematch (Oct 4, 2025; TKO at 1:20 of R1), then stopped late replacement Bogdan Guskov in R5 of the UFC Abu Dhabi main event (Jul 25, 2026). Pro record 21-2-1 (1 NC) per Sherdog and Wikipedia (ESPN lists 22-2-1). He is the #1 contender to champion Carlos Ulberg, who is rehabbing a reconstructed ACL and targeting early 2027. In September 2026 he publicly challenged Paulo Costa, who is in a contract dispute with the UFC; mid-October coverage still called that fight 'potential'. No bout booked and no injuries reported as of Nov 6, 2026.
status.ranking: #1 light heavyweight contender on the UFC media rankings updated Nov 3, 2026 (CBS Sports; ufcalendar.com mirror); #2 on the UFC/Meta algorithmic rankings updated Oct 31, 2026 (ufcalendar.com)

style.summary: A well-rounded, physically strong orthodox light heavyweight who chops at the body, pushes opponents onto the fence and grinds through clinch and top control. He is very hard to take down, and his head defense is excellent (opponents land 24% to the head). He gives up a lot of leg kicks and finishes few takedowns from open space.

moves.notes: Target groups follow fighters.json decayed sums: sig attempts 63.6% head, 24.1% body, 12.3% leg (career 69.3/20.8/9.9). The light heavyweight league split is about 75/14/11, so his body share is roughly 1.7x the league's. Kicks lead the body group as a judgment: his heavy body counts come in fights fought mostly at range (22/29 body vs Rakic, where 50 of his 55 sig landed at distance). ufcstats does not separate punches from kicks. Jab and cross share the top of the head group as a judgment; the hook (0.20) and uppercut (0.08) were raised slightly on Nov 6, 2026 because the Walker KO was a right hook followed by an uppercut (Cageside Press, Jan 13, 2024). Head kick is set at 0.1 because two of his UFC KOs came from kicks to the head (dataset method details). The knee is set at 0.12 for his clinch work (10.6% clinch share of sig landed). No spinning attacks are recorded. No technique-level breakdown of his striking was found as of Nov 6, 2026.

appearance.build: tall, long-limbed and lean rather than bulky (190.5 cm; 205.5 lb at the Jul 2026 weigh-in): broad but slightly sloping shoulders, flat pecs, narrow waist, long slim legs and calves; dark body hair on the chest, abdomen, forearms and legs

appearance.facial_hair: dense full beard, clearly auburn/reddish-brown (#4a2414) and warmer than his hair, about 5-7 cm under the chin with a rounded-square bottom; short moustache blending into it
appearance.tattoos: none visible in any photo (front and both sides; the back is only partly seen)
appearance.kit: red UFC-issued board shorts with dark-red tiger-stripe print, white slashes, black waistband and crypto.com logo (Mar 2025 and Jul 2026 ESPN cutouts; ANKALAEV lettering on the 2025 pair); red shorts with a white checkered waistband panel in the Jul 2026 fight; black shorts at weigh-ins
appearance.notes: Copied from the photo-based likeness sheet data/likeness/magomed-ankalaev.json (as of Nov 6, 2026; 9 photos, 2018-2026), which is the better source for the avatar: it has colour hexes (skin tone #eca691, neutral-to-warm undertone with pink, light freckles), face notes and morphs. Its warnings: keep the beard visibly redder than the near-black hair, keep the fringe over the forehead, and keep him slim and long-limbed, not a bodybuilder. The earlier 'broad and heavy-framed' build line was wrong.

engine_notes.note: Opponents land 1.58 leg strikes per minute on him (decayed), against a light heavyweight league average of about 0.72. Leg kicks are the reliable way to score on him.
Head defense is elite: opponents land 23.9% of head strikes against him (decayed), against about 41% across the league.
Takedown defense is 92.5% decayed and 87.5% career. Opponents control him only 1.9% of the time, while he controls 27% of fight time.
His output dropped to 3 sig strikes in each of R4 and R5 vs Guskov while he held top control before the R5 finish. Low sig counts in late rounds can mean control, not fatigue.
